There are four steps in a card transaction: (i) initiation; (ii) authentication; (iii) authorisation; and (iv)
When a card payment transaction is made, the payment processing goes through stages below:
- Card Payment Authorization — This is when the transaction is verified by the card company. They check
the customer’s payment card validity and whether they have sufficient funds for the transaction. When
everything’s fine, the transaction is then authorized and the total amount of transaction is deducted and
held from the customer’s credit line account. Note that the money is not transferred to the merchant
account yet. This is when credit card capture comes in.
- Card Payment Capture — This is when a merchant “tells” the card company that transaction has been
completed between them and the customer. Now, money can be transferred.
